summary.text: Mike Collins is the Republican nominee and the U.S. Representative for Georgia's 10th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A Jackson, Georgia, businessman who co-founded a trucking company, he lost a 2014 House runoff before winning the seat eight years later. He is running for the Senate on his House record, including authoring the Laken Riley Act, and support for President Trump's agenda.

paragraphs.text: Born July 2, 1967, and raised in Jackson, Georgia, where he still lives, according to his House website and Wikipedia; he is the son of former U.S. Rep. Mac Collins.
Earned a business degree from Georgia State University in 1990.
Co-founded a trucking company with his wife, Leigh Ann, in the early 1990s that, according to his House website, now employs more than 100 Georgians.
Served on the board and as chairman of one of Georgia's largest credit unions and as president of his local chamber of commerce, per his House website.
Ran for Georgia's 10th District in 2014, finishing second in the Republican primary and losing the runoff to Jody Hice, 54.3% to 45.7%.
Won the 2022 Republican primary runoff over Vernon Jones (74.5% to 25.5%) and the general election over Democrat Tabitha Johnson-Green (64.5% to 35.5%); he was re-elected in 2024.

Serves on the Natural Resources, Transportation and Infrastructure (chair of the Water Resources and Environment subcommittee), and Science, Space, and Technology committees in the 2025-2026 Congress.

According to material from his campaign website, he passed the TRANQ Act and the Laken Riley Act, the latter signed into law in January 2025, and was appointed to the House Whip Team. He and Leigh Ann have three grown children and four grandchildren, per his House website.
